Transposed convolution: learned upsampling.

Enlarges the sample by the stride (PyTorch ConvTranspose2d rules: (H-1)\*stride - 2\*padding + kernel + output_padding) with out_channels channels. The input channel count comes from the layer before it. Runs on ArrayFire.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Category | [Upsampling](../categories/upsampling.md) |
| Status | Runs |
| Search words | convtranspose, transposed, convolution, upsample |

## Settings

| Group | Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Transposed Convolution | Input Channels | `in_channels` | Integer | `64` | `1-1048576` | The run | Expected input channels (the compiler uses the actual count) Required. |
| Transposed Convolution | Output Channels | `out_channels` | Integer | `32` | `1-1048576` | The run | Output channels. Required. |
| Transposed Convolution | Kernel Size | `kernel_size` | Integer | `3` | `1-1048576` | The run | Square kernel size. Required. |
| Transposed Convolution | Stride | `stride` | Integer | `2` | `1-1048576` | The run | Spatial stride (the upsampling factor) Required. |
| Transposed Convolution | Padding | `padding` | Integer | `1` | `0-1048576` | The run | Symmetric input padding. Required. |
| Transposed Convolution | Output Padding | `output_padding` | Integer | `1` | `0-1048576` | The run | Extra size on one side of the output (smaller than the stride) Required. |
| Transposed Convolution | Bias | `use_bias` | On / off | `true` |   | The run | Adds a learned value per output channel. Turn it off when a BatchNorm follows (the BatchNorm's shift does the same job), as torchvision's ResNet and MobileNet do. |
| Fine-tuning | Frozen | `frozen` | On / off | `false` |   | The run | Keeps this layer's weights as they are while the rest of the model trains: no gradient step, no weight decay, no optimizer memory. Use it on layers that start from a weights file (fine-tuning), then turn it off to train them too. |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).
